data.title: NZ shares end choppy session lower after election results
data.description:
Key points:
  • New Zealand shares end lower after ruling coalition falls short of majority
  • Australia miners post weekly gain of 5.2%
  • WiseTech Global shares jump over 15% on trading update

By Nichiket Sunil

New Zealand shares ended a choppy session lower on Friday after the country's ruling coalition fell short of majority, raising the prospects of prolonged coalition negotiations, while Australian equities posted their best week in nearly four months.

New Zealand's benchmark S&P/NZX 50 index ended down 0.5% at 13,911.36 points.

New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon will seek the support of the centrist Opportunity Party to keep his ruling centre-right coalition in power after falling short of a majority, raising risks of a fresh election if the parties cannot overcome policy differences.

"Markets dislike uncertainty, and we're now facing the prospect of potentially prolonged coalition negotiations, questions around the composition of the next government and, importantly, what that means for future policy settings," said Greg Smith, investment specialist at Generate KiwiSaver.

Meanwhile, Australia's S&P/ASX 200 index closed up 0.8% at 8,833.60 points, gaining 2% for the week as appetite for AI-linked assets recovered.

Miners rose 2.4%, taking weekly gains to 5.2%, their biggest since mid-August, recouping some of last week's losses triggered by a global tech selloff.

Recovering copper prices, supported by renewed optimism over AI-related demand for the metal used in data centre construction, lifted BHP and Rio Tinto by 2% and 1.5%, respectively.

Gold stocks gained 3.8%, taking weekly gains to nearly 6.7% as bullion recovered. Northern Star Resources surged 3.8%.

Shares of logistics software maker WiseTech Global soared over 15% on reaffirming its annual revenue target and strong revenue from CargoWise, its flagship software.

The boost comes as a reprieve for the firm, with legal and governance concerns weighing on shares, which are down nearly 21% this year.

WiseTech shares boosted the technology sub-index 3.6%.

data.title: European Shares Poised To Open Higher
data.description:
BRUSSELS/FRANKFURT/PARIS (dpa-AFX) - European stocks are set to open on a firm note on Friday despite long-term anxieties surrounding the AI trade, lingering Middle East tensions and expectations for higher-for-longer interest rates.

Global technology stocks stabilized after recent string of losses due to dip-buying.

Amid tighter U.S. export controls, Nvidia is not allowing orders of computer servers containing its artificial intelligence chips to be shipped to four Southeast Asian countries, the Financial Times reported Thursday.

On the geopolitical front, a strike on an oil refinery in Saudi Arabia's southern Jazan region heightened concerns over supply disruptions from the Middle East.

Earlier, there was an attack on the Ras Tanura oil hub in the Persian Gulf, and a tanker was hit in the Strait of Hormuz.

Two Italian nationals were killed on Thursday in a drone attack on the Gulf nation of Kuwait. Clarifying that it had no involvement in the incident, Tehran warned against attempts to widen confrontations.

Separately, Israel said it is ready to strike Iran 'at any moment' even without U.S. military involvement, heightening concerns over a potential escalation of the conflict in the region.

Late Thursday, U.S. President Donald Trump said on PBS that the United States has 'victory at hand' in the Iran conflict, while expressing uncertainty over whether Iran would accept the opportunity for a deal.

Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghci said that Tehran's immediate focus was on strengthening the country's resilience against the pressures that enemies apply through various means.

Closer home, Spain goes to the polls on Sunday in an early parliamentary election.

Latest polls put the conservative Popular Party ahead of incumbent PM Pedro Sanchez's Socialists.

Spanish central banking veteran Pablo Hernandez de Cos has been chosen to succeed Christine Lagarde as the next European Central Bank President.

U.S. stock futures ticked higher ahead of a shortened Wall Street session following the Thanksgiving holiday.

Asian markets were mostly higher amid easing concerns over U.S. trade tensions.

Treasuries fell, with yield on the benchmark 10-year note rising two basis points to 4.87 percent as trading resumed after the Thanksgiving holiday. The U.S. dollar hovered below a 22-month peak as AI worries eased.

Gold jumped more than 2 percent to $3,651 on ounce after sinking to a 15-month low earlier in the week. Amid persistent inflation and growing volatility, investors looked ahead to next month's Federal Reserve meeting for signals on the path of borrowing costs.

Brent crude futures surged toward $97 a barrel and were on track for their first weekly gain this month following recent attacks on Middle eastern energy facilities and tankers.

On Thursday, European stocks staged a broad-based rally amid signs that Washington would respect the 15 percent levy the European Union had concluded with the United States.

The pan-European STOXX 600 jumped 1.8 percent after falling 1.1 percent on Wednesday.

The German DAX rallied 2.1 percent, France's CAC 40 gained 1.6 percent and the U.K.'s FTSE 100 surged 1.8 percent.
